tagline.text: A quiet pair of waterfalls hidden in the forest above Daranak Falls

location.label: Location
location.text: Tanay, Rizal, inside the Daranak Falls resort area

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~1,500 (per person, round trip by public transport from Manila)

children.text: Batlag Falls is a pair of waterfalls deep in the forest inside the Daranak Falls resort area in Tanay, Rizal. A paved path with steps from Daranak reaches it in about 10–15 minutes, and with far fewer visitors it is a peaceful day-trip swimming spot near Manila.
Batlag Falls lies in Tanay, Rizal, about
55km
east of Manila. It is not a stand-alone park with its own gate. It sits in the forest upstream of the already famous
Daranak Falls
resort, further up the creek. Visitors agree that when navigating with a map app, it is easier to search for Daranak Falls rather than Batlag.

There are two waterfalls here. One is a smaller cascade that spreads out thin like a veil, and the other is a somewhat larger fall with an unusual rock formation, and each has its own pool at the bottom. One mountaineering blog gives the height as about
. You can swim in each pool, but there are sharp rocks on the bottom, so it is safer to keep your shoes on even in the water.

If Daranak Falls is a family outing spot with a wide pool, shops and cottages, Batlag is less developed and feels much more natural. The facilities are basic, and visitors often complain about the state of the restrooms, but in return it is quiet enough on a weekday morning that you can almost have the falls to yourself. Pairing it with Daranak, seeing Daranak first and then walking up to Batlag, fills a half day nicely.

Shaded by the forest on the slopes of the Sierra Madre, the water is cool, and the color of the pools shifts with the light from pale sky blue to turquoise to emerald. Right after a typhoon or in the middle of the rainy season the water turns muddy easily, so go in the dry season if you want clear water. You pay an entrance fee once at the Daranak gate and again at the Batlag entrance, so the total can feel higher than expected on a first visit. Reviews from 2025 report a combined total of about ₱175~180 per person, so bring plenty of cash.

The smaller fall on the left drops in a thin, veil-like stream, while the larger fall on the right has an unusual rock formation. Both have a pool below, so you can step into them one after the other and compare the atmosphere.
Follow the Batlag signs near the Daranak Falls pool and walk up the uphill cement path and steps, and you arrive in about
10–15 minutes
. There are steep stretches that leave you out of breath, but it is not rough, and because the path has been improved you can avoid muddy trails.

Many reviews say the water is cooler and clearer than at Daranak. The pool at the waterfall is relatively large and evenly deep, while locals say the pool on the other side is less than half the size and deeper. Life vests can be rented if you need one.
A little further on from the falls, there is said to be a deeper, bluer lagoon. There are no signs, so ask a lifeguard for directions, and wear sturdy shoes because the path is slippery.
Further up the creek behind the falls, the water is said to be even clearer. Just after rain the water level changes quickly, so check with the local caretaker that the section is safe before you go.

You can rent a table and a shed to eat a packed lunch and rest. There are not many of them, and some reviews say they cost more than at Daranak, so on weekends it is best to arrive early and secure a spot.
Batlag is right above Daranak, so once you are in you can see both falls in one visit. A good order is to swim and take photos at Daranak and then walk up to Batlag for the quiet.
The falls dropping through the shade of the trees and the color of the water make for good photos. Soft early-morning light is best, and for drone shooting, ask the local authorities first.

items.title: Day-trip route
items.subtitle: Two waterfalls, from Daranak to Batlag

children.text: Take a Tanay-bound van from the Starmall van terminal on Shaw Boulevard in Manila. Vans leave when full, so it is best to go early.
Get off at the Tanay public market and take a tricycle to the Daranak Falls entrance. It takes about
20–30 minutes
Pay the entrance fee at the Daranak gate, then look around the falls pool and have a light swim.
Follow the Batlag signs up the uphill path, pay the Batlag entrance fee at the small store at the entrance, and enter the falls.
Swim in the pools of the two falls, and ask a lifeguard where the secret lagoon is.
Eat the lunch you brought and rest in a shed.
Come back down to Daranak, collect your belongings and head into Tanay town.
Have a snack in Tanay town and look around the old town and church.
Take a van back to Manila. Allow for rush-hour traffic.
There are slippery rocks around Batlag, so aqua shoes or sandals with firm soles are best. Adjust the schedule to the weather and the water level.
Leave Manila by car and head to Tanay via Marcos Highway or the C-6 direction.
Pay the entrance fee at the Daranak gate and go straight up to Batlag while it is empty.
See the secret lagoon first, then the large and small falls in that order.
Come back down to Daranak, see the falls before the crowds arrive, and have lunch.
Some reviewers say they almost had the falls to themselves on weekday mornings. This route can still get crowded on weekends, holidays and summer vacation.

items.title: From Manila by van and tricycle

children.text: Vans to Tanay run from the Starmall van terminal on Shaw Boulevard in Manila (near EDSA Crossing-Shaw). The fare is about
, and the trip takes
2–3 hours
depending on traffic.
The van drops you near the Tanay public market. From there, hire a tricycle to the Daranak entrance. It takes about
20–30 minutes
, and the fare is reported at about
(₱200 per trip for up to 4 passengers; round-trip hire ₱250~350 reported) depending on the number of passengers. Haggling is needed, so agree on the fare first.
After paying the entrance fee at the Daranak entrance, walk past the falls and follow the Batlag signs uphill.
Fares vary by period, so confirm locally. Ride-hailing apps may not reach the falls.
From Manila, go east via C-5 and Ortigas Avenue through Taytay and Morong, or take Marcos Highway through Antipolo to Tanay. With light traffic it takes about
2 hours
For navigation, it is safer to enter Daranak Falls rather than Batlag Falls. There is a parking lot, but it gets crowded on weekends.
Follow the Batlag signs near the Daranak Falls pool and walk up the cement path and steps, and you arrive in about
10–15 minutes
. There are steep stretches, but it is not rough.
In some cases the Batlag entrance fee is collected at a small store near the entrance.
The water is clearest generally during the dry season from December to May. The paths are less slippery and the water is less likely to turn cloudy.

From June to November it is the rainy season, so the water muddies easily, and right after heavy rain the water level can rise suddenly. Follow the caretakers' instructions then, and for safety do not enter if the water has turned brown or is rising.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

There is no lodging inside Batlag, and although there are small shops near the falls, they charge tourist prices. One visitor reported almost no shops, so we recommend bringing a packed lunch and drinking water. Restrictions on plastic and styrofoam containers have been announced at times, so check at the entrance.

For lodging, use the town of Tanay, which is close to Daranak Falls, or a nearby resort. Among long-known options, the restaurants around the old town of Tanay and the market food are reliable. There are records that camping was once allowed, but the rules may have changed, so check the latest notice.

Around the Tanay public market there are stalls selling freshwater fish dishes caught in Laguna de Bay, fruit and rice-cake snacks. On the way back from the falls, it is also nice to stop by for a warm soup dish or a sweet snack. Opening hours differ from shop to shop, so keep in mind that some may close early in the late afternoon and after.
In your map app, enter Daranak Falls as the destination rather than Batlag.
Early weekday mornings are the quietest. On weekends, holidays and summer vacation, arrive early.
There are sharp rocks on the bottom, so wear aqua shoes or sandals with firm soles.
Entrance and rental fees are often paid in cash, so bring plenty of small change.
If you are not a confident swimmer, rent a life vest and stay out of the deep end.
Bring a packed lunch, drinking water, a change of clothes, a waterproof bag and a trash bag, and carry your trash out with you.
Before heading to the secret lagoon or upstream, ask a lifeguard about the route and whether it is safe.
Reviews mention poorly maintained restrooms, so bring tissue and hand sanitizer.
Vans leave when full, so check the return van time in advance and come down into town before dark.
Wear shoes that can get wet, and keep socks and a change of clothes in a separate plastic bag.
After rain the water can turn brown and the level can rise suddenly, so do not enter the water then.
There are many sharp, slippery rocks on the pool floors and edges, so it is easy to fall and get hurt.
The uphill path is steep, so children and older visitors should walk slowly and children should be watched closely.
Phone signal is weak in some stretches, so stay with your group and head down early.
The Daranak entrance is usually reported open daily 08:00~17:00 (2022 and 2024 guides). Entrance fees and operating hours change with local conditions, so check the latest notice.
Keep valuables in a waterproof bag or use a locker, and do not pick plants or write on the rocks.
It lies right below in the same resort area. It is about a
10–15 minute
walk and has a wide pool and facilities.

blocks.title: Tanay Old Town and San Ildefonso Church

children.text: It is in the town where you take the tricycle to the falls, so it is easy to stop by on the way there or back.
Another natural attraction in Rizal that requires advance reservations. Plan a separate trip to visit it.
A blog has presented it as a full-day route combined with Batlag and Daranak. Check locally whether it is open and what it costs.
